Close Call could show the same odds three lines in a row. Tonight HOOD Dec 11 (stock $67.36) said 52.1% to close above $66, 52.1% above $67 and 52.1% above $68, as if it couldn't close between $66 and $68. The cause: when the overnight option prices were noisy, the app kept the odds in order by giving the noisy strikes one shared value. Now that shared value sits at the middle and the lines either side read a straight line between their neighbours, so the odds still never go up as the line goes up, and they now fall at every line. Clean option prices give the same numbers as before. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

Built the 'Put it on your home screen' card (the Scout's proposal for your mobile-app question). After someone has made their first call, Home offers to add MarketPlayground to their phone's home screen: one tap on Android, the two Share steps on iPhone (where alerts only work from the home screen). 'Not now' hides it for 30 days; it's also on the Account page. It only counts, no names: how many were offered it, added it, said not now, and opened the app from their home screen. You'll see those last-7-day numbers at the top of this page. Right now 0 people have alerts on, so this tells us whether people install before we pay for app stores.

Close Call's odds went almost flat right at the stock's price. After tonight's close NVDA Dec 4 (stock $164.85) said 55.5% to close above $162.50 and 54.1% above $165, but 59.2% above $160 and 47.9% above $167.50. The cause: where the option smile switches from put prices to call prices, the two disagreed by 2.6 volatility points, and the app read that jump as real skew. Now, near the stock's price, put and call prices are blended, so the odds keep falling steadily through the price. When puts and calls agree, nothing changes. Tonight's NVDA numbers still use the smile saved this afternoon; the fix shows from tomorrow's 3-4 PM ET save, and in market hours right away. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

Close Call's odds could still go up as the line went up during market hours, because some lines read one option spread, some one volatility and some the smoothed option curve. Live this afternoon SPY Dec 4 said 34.6% to close above $735 but 37.4% above $740. Now every line reads the same smoothed curve for its date whenever the option prices allow it, market open or closed, so a higher line never shows higher odds, and YES still costs about the odds shown. On clean prices the curve matches the listed spreads to within 0.1 points. One spread or one volatility is used only when the curve can't be read. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

Close Call's odds could go up as the line went up. Live this afternoon, AMD Dec 18 said 63.7% to close above $410 but 63.8% above $420, and Dec 11 said 31.1% above $480 but 35.5% above $490. Fixed part of it: the odds read from the option prices now come from one curve for each date, kept in order and built from the same prices for every line, and YES still costs about the odds shown. After market hours every line reads that curve, so tonight's ladders fall line by line. Still open in market hours: some lines are read a different way (one listed spread, or one volatility) and can sit a few points out of order (SPY Dec 4: 34.6% above $735 but 37.4% above $740). Next run I'll make every line use the ordered curve when it can be read. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

replies.re: Make a reel of the new search feature (live chat)
replies.body: Promo v7 made and sent to you (34s). It opens on four real searches: a word (lithium), a question (why is nvidia up?), a company (Costco), a ticker (TSLA). Then a typo gets fixed, the AI story, who it moves, practice money, and the scorecard. While making it I found questions didn't work in search ('why is nvidia up' found nothing). Fixed: a question now searches its subject, and a company name or capitalised ticker anywhere in a sentence brings up that company.

Search polish, part 1 (the Chair's ask). I tried 12 searches on the live site. Typos found nothing at all: 'nvdia' and 'teslla' showed an empty page that offered to spend an AI story on the misspelling. Now, when a search finds nothing, it tries the likely spelling and says so: 'Nothing found for “nvdia”, so showing results for “nvidia”', with a 'Search “nvdia” as typed' link. It only fixes words it doesn't know that sit very close to a company name or a word in this week's stories, so real words with no story (like 'uranium') are left alone. Also, 'costco earnings' now shows the Costco card and headlines like 'costco' does. Searches still take about half a second.

Close Call gave odds that went up as the line went up when the market was closed. Before Monday's open, TSLA at $366.66 said 63% to close above $350 but 68% above $360; AMD and META had the same problem. Overnight, the free feed's option quotes get very wide (one NVDA option was quoted at $14.34 to buy back and $24.36 to buy, against $13.24 / $13.66 once the market opened), and stocks move before the open while options don't update, so the app was reading odds out of noise. Now, during market hours, the app saves each date's option prices from tight quotes only, plus a snapshot of the 15 big stocks in the last hour of trading. When the market is closed, the odds come from that saved set, moved with the stock's latest price, and the screen says so (e.g. 'saved in the last session, Fri 3:13 PM ET'). Every line now comes from the same numbers, so the odds fall as the line rises. Market-hours odds are unchanged. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

replies.re: Let's start thinking of making this a mobile app vs online app
replies.body: The Chair has answered this with the options. From the build side: the site already works at phone size, so an installable home-screen app (PWA) is the smallest first step whenever you want it. Just say the word and I'll build it.
